subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 19-year-old man with short stature, bilateral sensorineural hearing loss, and recurrent stroke-like episodes has lactic acidosis and ragged red fibers on muscle biopsy. Genetic testing shows a homoplasmic point mutation in the mitochondrial gene encoding tRNA-Leu(UUR). Structural analysis of the mutant tRNA shows loss of the T-psi-C sequence with an otherwise intact cloverleaf structure, an intact anticodon loop, and an intact 3'-CCA terminus.
question: Loss of this sequence would most directly impair which of the following functions?

options.text: Recognition of the tRNA by its specific aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase
Binding of the tRNA to the ribosome
Covalent attachment of the amino acid to the 3' end
Codon-anticodon base pairing in the A site

explanation_correct: The T-arm contains the T-psi-C sequence, which is necessary for tRNA-ribosome binding and tethers the tRNA molecule to the ribosome during translation. The D-arm instead carries dihydrouridine residues required for recognition by the correct aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase, so the arms serve distinct roles.

explanation_incorrect.A: Recognition by aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase depends primarily on the D-arm, which contains dihydrouridine residues and is intact in this patient.
explanation_incorrect.C: Amino acid attachment requires the invariant CCA sequence at the 3' end, which is described as intact.
explanation_incorrect.D: Codon-anticodon pairing depends on the anticodon loop, which is structurally separate from the T-arm.
explanation_incorrect.E: Peptidyl transferase activity is catalyzed by ribosomal RNA (a ribozyme) rather than by tRNA.

educationalObjective: The T-arm (T-psi-C sequence) of tRNA is required for binding to the ribosome, whereas the D-arm mediates recognition by aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase.
